findings.claim: Across the changed locations, forEach callbacks were made async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar. findings.claim: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts around line 589, the awaited appStore lookup and PaymentService instantiation happen outside the try/catch. A failure there bypasses handleRefundError and throws out of the cancellation/refund flow.

verifier.reason: In handleCancelBooking.ts:589-596, `await appStore[...]` and `new PaymentService(paymentAppCredential)` both sit before the `try` at line 597, which only wraps `paymentInstance.refund()`, so a rejected import or a throwing constructor skips handleRefundError (lines 600-604) and propagates out of the handler. findings.claim: In packages/app-store/index.ts, appStore values are `import("./x")` expressions evaluated when the object literal is built. Importing appStore therefore loads all app packages immediately rather than lazily on key access.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/index.ts:3-30, every value is a bare `import("./x")` call inside the object literal, so all 28 dynamic imports start as soon as the module is evaluated. Nothing defers them to key access (no getter or `() => import(...)` thunk), so the change only makes loading async, not lazy.

findings.claim: Developer docs still instruct adding a static import to packages/app-store/index.ts, while the convention is now `appname: import("./appname")`.

verifier.reason: apps/docs/pages/developer/app-store.mdx:43 and :56 still tell developers to import the app into packages/app-store/index.ts and then add it to the appStore object. The patch removed every top-level import there and replaced them with `appname: import("./appname")` entries (change.patch lines 26-114), but it did not update the docs. A static import would still work, because awaiting a value that is not a promise just returns it, so the stale docs are only a nit.

findings.claim: In packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15, the awaited appStore import has no error handling, so a failed dynamic import surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

verifier.reason: getCalendar is async (packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:9), so a rejected import awaited at line 15 rejects the promise getCalendar returns, and callers that await it receive the error (e.g. CalendarManager.ts createEvent/deleteEvent, handleCancelBooking). Passing the error up instead of catching it locally is normal, and it is not an unhandled rejection at this line. Any unhandled rejection would come from callers such as the `forEach(async ...)` in reschedule.ts, or from the eager `import()` calls in app-store/index.ts, not from getCalendar.ts:15.

findings.claim: An await of an import has no try/catch around it to handle import failures.

verifier.reason: The patch adds bare awaits on dynamic import() promises with no try/catch, for example packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15 (`await appStore[...]`), getVideoAdapters in packages/core/videoClient.ts, and the payment lookups in packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts and deletePayment.ts. This is a minor issue because a missing module would also have crashed the old static imports at load time, and index.ts starts every import() immediately.

findings.claim: The for loop in getVideoAdapters loads adapters serially rather than in parallel.

verifier.reason: The loop in packages/core/videoClient.ts:24-26 does await each `appStore[...]` entry one after another, but each entry is a promise created when the module loads (packages/app-store/index.ts:3-11 calls `import("./...")` eagerly). So every module is already loading at the same time, and awaiting them in order takes about as long as Promise.all would; the loading is not serial.

findings.claim: A failing app-module import now rejects at module evaluation with no handler attached until a request awaits that key. It therefore surfaces as an unhandledRejection instead of a catchable import error.

verifier.reason: The patch changes packages/app-store/index.ts:87-114 so every app is loaded with an eager `import("./x")` when the module is evaluated, and nothing attaches a handler to those promises until a consumer awaits that key (e.g. getCalendar.ts:17, videoClient.ts:247). A failing import therefore rejects with no handler and raises unhandledRejection, where the old static `import * as` made the importing module fail to load with an ordinary import error.
